Subject: Unusual micro-billing rollups in November invoices — request for correction

Hi Soojin,

Quick note from our finance team: the November marketplace payout shows a large withheld amount tied to EU VAT reclassification. We dug into the invoice and found hundreds of very small line items (~€0.02–€0.50) that appear to have been bucketized across multiple seller-entity mappings instead of being rolled up under our single NimbleCloud VAT entity. The resulting VAT calculation looks misapplied which triggered a withholding on the payout.

Attached: small sample PDF of the invoice lines (NimbleCloud_invoice_sample_NOV2028.pdf) and the raw metering export we pulled (nimblecloud_metering_lines_202811.csv).

Can Redwood confirm:
- why these micro-usage rows were split into separate ledger buckets?
- whether VAT grouping should have aggregated by our EU VAT ID before applying tax?

We need an estimate of the value at risk and any temporary credit while you investigate — our payroll window is next Tuesday and this withholding will materially impact our payroll.

Thanks,
Ellie Summers
Head of Finance 
NimbleCloud Ltd

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: ACTION: reconcile microbilling rollup mapping for NimbleCloud (NimbleCloud Ltd)

Quick update from my pass this morning:

Findings (preliminary):
- The ingestion pipeline introduced a change to "micro-batch window" on 2028-11-05 (commit: ad3f7c) that causes very small events to be sharded by 'storage_zone' before aggregation. That change unintentionally ran prior to a SKU mapping rule we deploy for EU VAT grouping.
- As a result ~28% of micro-lines were attributed to a temporary intermediate bucket (storage_zone) which then got emitted as separate invoice lines; when downstream VAT assignment ran it treated them as distinct seller entities.
- Aggregating by VAT ID (GB999999973) and customer_id reduces the number of invoice lines by ~5,800 and corrects VAT assignment for those rows. The net delta I compute is ~€14,200 in VAT overstatement (which is likely the driver of the payout withholding).

Attachments: redwood_metering_diff_snapshot.png, nimblecloud_reconciled_delta_20281119.csv

Proposed short-term remediation:
1) Apply a retroactive aggregation pass for November invoices that groups micro-lines by vat_id + customer_id before VAT tagging, regenerate VAT summaries for impacted invoices, and issue credit memos where appropriate. (Owner: Rafael / Marissa)
2) Rollback the micro-batch window change or patch the ingestion writer to ensure VAT mapping runs prior to sharding by storage_zone (Owner: Logan)
3) Issue a provisional credit to NimbleCloud for up to €15k pending formal approval from Finance Ops (Owner: Soojin)

I'll drop the reconciled CSV to the evidence folder and create a JIRA subtask for the ingestion revert.

Rafael
Senior Billing Engineer

Hi Ellie — thanks again for the samples and patience. Quick summary and next steps: 

What we found:
- Root cause: an internal change to micro-batch sharding (2028-11-05) caused some very small meter events to be emitted into an intermediate bucket prior to VAT-mapping. That led to fragmentation of micro-usage lines and incorrect VAT assignment for a subset of rows.
- Impact: Rafael's reconciliation shows ~5,800 micro-lines affected with an estimated VAT overstatement of ~€14,200. That amount aligns with the withheld payout amount your team saw.

Our remediation plan (timeline):
- Immediate (today): we've created JIRA-BILL-4127 and pushed reconciled CSV and evidence to the shared Drive. Rafael and Marissa will produce credit memos for impacted invoices and a bundled remediation package for your accounts team (ETA 48 hours).
- Near-term (48–72 hours): we will run a retroactive aggregation pass to regenerate VAT summaries and issue credit memos where applicable.
- System fix (next week): Logan will roll back the micro-batch window change or patch the writer so VAT grouping occurs before sharding.

Provisional credit: pending quick Finance Ops sign-off, we're prepared to issue a provisional credit up to €15,000 to mitigate your payroll impact while we complete the reissue. Please confirm that a provisional credit of up to €15k would be sufficient and provide the canonical EU VAT ID we should use (confirming GB999999973).

I'll keep you updated hourly as Rafael and Marissa complete the reconciliation. We appreciate your patience and will prioritize the payout unblock.

Best,
